name: Judicial bias

subjectOf.text: Conducting judicial proceedings through interpreters is cumbersome and confusing and creates a perceived bias in favor of litigants and lawyers fluent in the language of the proceedings, which is a barrier to exporting adjudication.
subjectOf.abstract: Conducting judicial proceedings through interpreters, however, is cumbersome and confusing, and also creates a perceived bias in favor of litigants and lawyers who are fluent in the language of the proceedings.
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681
scope_conditions: Member States whose courts do not conduct proceedings in English

subjectOf.text: Fear of judicial bias operates through risk premiums: because investors and managers are uncertain how foreign judges will behave and may assume the worst, they price a decision to incorporate in another Member State higher.
subjectOf.abstract: Risk premiums charged by actors often reflect both bounded rationality and incomplete information, and managers and investors thus may put a higher price on a decision to incorporate in another Member State.
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681
scope_conditions: bounded rationality and incomplete information about foreign judges

subjectOf.text: If statutes are unbundled from adjudication the judicial bias problem largely disappears, because statutes are at least facially neutral and discriminatory statutes would violate the EU treaty.
subjectOf.abstract: If on the other hand, statutes are unbundled from adjudication, this problem largely disappears because statutes are at least facially neutral
subjectOf.citation: Christian Kirchner, Richard W. Painter, Wulf A. Kaal, Regulatory Competition in EU Corporate Law after Inspire Art Unbundling Delaware's Product for Euro (2004). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=617681
scope_conditions: EU law, under which discriminatory national provisions violate freedom of establishment
